blocks.text: In a piston engine the big end of the connecting rod moves in a circle while the small end moves in a straight line, and the rod between them both translates and rotates. Knowing how fast each end moves, and how fast the rod turns, starts from a single equation that links the velocities of any two points on a rigid body.

blocks.markdown: General plane motion is the sum of a translation and a rotation. If two points $A$ and $B$ are fixed in the same rigid body, the distance $AB$ cannot change, so the only way $A$ can move relative to $B$ is by rotating about it. With $\boldsymbol\omega$ the angular velocity of the body (rad/s) and $\mathbf r_{A/B}$ the position of $A$ relative to $B$ (m):

blocks.caption: $\mathbf v_{A/B}=\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$ has magnitude $\omega\,AB$ and is perpendicular to the line $AB$.

blocks.title: Rigid-body constraint
blocks.text: Since $|AB|$ is constant, the components of $\mathbf v_A$ and $\mathbf v_B$ **along** the line $AB$ are equal. The difference of the two velocities is perpendicular to $AB$. This single fact often gives an unknown speed immediately, and then the perpendicular difference gives $\omega$.

blocks.title: Link with sliding end
blocks.prompt: A link $AB$ of length 0.8 m is inclined at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal with $A$ above and to the right of $B$. End $A$ moves vertically upward at 2.0 m/s and $B$ is constrained to move horizontally. Find the angular velocity of the link and the speed of $B$.

steps.text: Relative position, with $B$ at the origin: $\mathbf r_{A/B}=(0.6928,\ 0.40)$ m. Unknowns: $v_B$ (horizontal) and $\omega$ (counterclockwise positive).

blocks.answer: $\omega=2.89$ rad/s counterclockwise and $v_B=1.15$ m/s in the $+x$ direction.

blocks.markdown: **Rolling without slip.** A wheel of radius $R$ rolling without slip on a fixed surface has its contact point instantaneously at rest. Taking the centre $G$ as the reference, $v_G=R\omega$, so $\omega=v_G/R$. The velocity of any rim point is $\mathbf v_P=\mathbf v_G+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{P/G}$. The contact point has $\mathbf v=0$, the top has $2v_G$ in the direction of travel, and a point at angle $\varphi$ from the top has speed $2v_G\cos(\varphi/2)$.

blocks.title: Point on a rolling wheel
blocks.prompt: A wheel of radius 0.40 m rolls without slip to the right with its centre at 6 m/s. Find the velocity of the rim point $60^\circ$ round from the top (towards the front of the wheel).

steps.text: Relative position of the point: $\mathbf r_{P/G}=0.40(\sin60^\circ,\ \cos60^\circ)$. Clockwise rotation gives $\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r=(6\cos60^\circ,\ -6\sin60^\circ)$.

blocks.caption: Velocities of points of a rolling wheel with centre speed $v_G$.

blocks.markdown: **Link angular velocity from one end.** To find $\omega$ of a link whose end $A$ has a known velocity and whose other end $B$ is on a guide: (1) draw the known $\mathbf v_A$ and the known *direction* of $\mathbf v_B$; (2) use the component along $AB$ to find $v_B$, or write the two scalar equations of $\mathbf v_A=\mathbf v_B+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$; (3) the component of $\mathbf v_{A/B}$ perpendicular to $AB$ equals $\omega\,AB$.

blocks.title: Two unknowns, two equations
blocks.text: The vector equation gives two scalar equations. With the direction of one velocity known, the unknowns are one speed and $\omega$, and the system is closed. Check the sense of $\omega$ by the right-hand rule.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.text: Using the speed of $A$ in $v=\omega\,AB$ instead of the **relative** velocity, taking $v=R\omega$ for the top of a wheel, and mixing clockwise and counterclockwise signs in $\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r$.

points: For two points on a rigid body, $\mathbf v_A=\mathbf v_B+\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$, and the relative velocity is perpendicular to $AB$.
A rolling wheel has $\omega=v_G/R$; the contact point is at rest and the top moves at $2v_G$.
Angular velocity of a link follows from the perpendicular component of the relative velocity divided by the link length.

questions.stem: Two points $A$ and $B$ are fixed on a rigid body turning with angular velocity $\omega$. What is the magnitude and direction of the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$?

options.text: Zero, because both points are on the same body

distractorRationale.b: A length cannot change on a rigid body, so there is no relative velocity along $AB$.
distractorRationale.c: This has the wrong dimensions; the speed is $\omega$ times distance.
distractorRationale.d: Points on the same body can move relative to each other by rotation.

questions.explanation: The relative velocity of two points of a rigid body is $\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{A/B}$, which has magnitude $\omega\,AB$ and is perpendicular to $AB$.

questions.stem: A wheel of radius 0.45 m rolls without slipping on level ground with its centre moving at 9.0 m/s. Find the speed of the topmost point of the rim in m/s.
questions.explanation: The angular velocity is $\omega=9.0/0.45=20$ rad/s. The top is $2R$ from the contact point, so its speed is $20(0.90)=18$ m/s, twice the centre speed.

questions.stem: A car's wheels have radius 0.30 m and turn at 600 rev/min without slipping on the road. Find the speed of the car in m/s.
questions.explanation: The angular velocity is $\omega=600(2\pi)/60=62.83$ rad/s. The centre speed is $v=R\omega=0.30(62.83)=18.85$ m/s, which is about 68 km/h.

questions.stem: A rigid link has point $B$ moving at $\mathbf v_B=(4,\,1)$ m/s and rotates counterclockwise at 5 rad/s. Point $A$ is at $\mathbf r_{A/B}=(0.36,\,0.48)$ m from $B$. Find the speed of $A$ in m/s.
questions.explanation: $\boldsymbol\omega\times\mathbf r_{A/B}=5(-0.48,\,0.36)=(-2.4,\,1.8)$ m/s. Then $\mathbf v_A=(4-2.4,\,1+1.8)=(1.6,\,2.8)$ m/s and $|\mathbf v_A|=3.22$ m/s.

questions.stem: A link of length 0.90 m is inclined at $40^\circ$ to the horizontal. End $A$ moves vertically at 1.5 m/s and end $B$ slides along a horizontal guide. What is the angular velocity of the link?

distractorRationale.a: This is $v_A/AB$, using the full length instead of the horizontal projection.
distractorRationale.c: This uses the vertical projection $AB\sin40^\circ$ in place of the horizontal one.
distractorRationale.d: This multiplies the speed by $\cos40^\circ$ instead of dividing by it.

questions.explanation: Since $\mathbf v_B$ is horizontal, the vertical velocity of $A$ comes only from rotation: $v_A=\omega\,AB\cos40^\circ$. Then $\omega=1.5/(0.90\cos40^\circ)=2.18$ rad/s.

questions.stem: A wheel rolls without slipping with centre speed $v$. Which row correctly gives the speeds of its contact point and its topmost point?

distractorRationale.a: The contact point is at rest; only the centre moves at $v$.
distractorRationale.b: The top point is twice as far from the instantaneous centre as the wheel centre.
distractorRationale.d: The contact point of a non-slipping wheel has zero velocity.

questions.explanation: The contact point is the instantaneous centre. The centre is at distance $R$ and moves at $v=R\omega$, so the top at distance $2R$ moves at $2v$.

questions.stem: The velocity of $A$ relative to $B$ on a rigid link is found to have a component along the line $AB$. What does this indicate?

options.text: An error: for a rigid body the relative velocity has no component along $AB$
The link must be at its dead-centre position

questions.correctOptionText: An error: for a rigid body the relative velocity has no component along $AB$

distractorRationale.b: This could be true for a deformable link, but the question concerns a rigid body.
distractorRationale.c: Zero $\omega$ gives zero relative velocity altogether.
distractorRationale.d: Dead centres do not create relative velocity along the link.

questions.explanation: For a rigid link $|AB|$ is constant, so $\mathbf v_{A/B}\cdot\mathbf r_{A/B}=0$. A component along $AB$ signals an arithmetic or setup error.

questions.stem: A link $AB$ of length 0.50 m has end $A$ moving at 5.0 m/s directed $30^\circ$ above the $+x$ axis. The link makes $60^\circ$ with the $+x$ axis, and end $B$ is constrained to move along the $x$-axis. Find the magnitude of the angular velocity of the link in rad/s.
questions.explanation: Equal components along $AB$: $v_B\cos60^\circ=5\cos(30^\circ)\cos60^\circ+5\sin30^\circ\sin60^\circ=4.33$ so $v_B=8.66$ m/s. The relative velocity $\mathbf v_A-\mathbf v_B=(-4.33,\,2.5)$ has perpendicular component $5.0$ m/s, so $\omega=5.0/0.50=10$ rad/s.

questions.stem: State the relative velocity equation for two points on a rigid body and explain how it is used, together with the rigid-body constraint, to find the angular velocity of a link when the velocity of one end and only the direction of the other end's velocity are known.
markingGuide: Explains that $\mathbf v_{A/B}$ is perpendicular to $AB$ with magnitude $\omega\,AB$
Uses equal components of velocity along $AB$ to find the unknown end speed
Takes the perpendicular component of $\mathbf v_{A}-\mathbf v_{B}$ and divides by $AB$ to get $\omega$
Determines the sense of $\omega$ from the direction of $\mathbf v_{A/B}$ (right-hand rule)
questions.explanation: The vector equation yields two scalar equations, which close the problem when one speed and $\omega$ are unknown. The along-link equality is a quick shortcut to the unknown end speed.

questions.stem: Show that for a wheel of radius $R$ rolling without slip with centre speed $v$, a rim point at angle $\varphi$ from the top has speed $2v\cos(\varphi/2)$. Use this to give the speeds at the top, the contact point and the point level with the centre.
questions.explanation: The result agrees with the instantaneous-centre view, because the chord from the contact point to a rim point at angle $\varphi$ from the top has length $2R\cos(\varphi/2)$ and the speed is $\omega$ times that length.
